strengths: The paper introduces PriVi, a novel 424-hour primate-centric video pretraining dataset, successfully addressing the critical domain gap and data scarcity in wild animal behavior analysis.
A well-designed, automated curation pipeline is proposed, leveraging CLIP embedding-based relevance filtering and zero-shot primate detection to clean noisy web and field recordings.
The paper presents a carefully tailored, deep yet narrow supervised attentive classifier that successfully prevents overfitting when evaluation is performed on small-scale downstream datasets.

Extensive experimental results show consistent and substantial improvements, establishing new state-of-the-art performance across four major primate behavior benchmarks (ChimpACT, BaboonLand, PanAf500, ChimpBehave) while outperforming much larger models.
Rigorous ablations demonstrate the value of each component, including the data subsets, relevance filtering, primate-centric cropping, and the proposed lightweight classifier head.
weaknesses: Due to privacy and ongoing research constraints, 14% of the curated dataset (camera trap footage) cannot be shared publicly, which slightly hinders full exact replication of the pretraining data.
The downstream evaluation relies on ground-truth bounding boxes for cropping, which might simplify the problem compared to a fully joint detection-and-recognition system in real-world deployment.
The manual selection process of 19 YouTube playlists could benefit from more detailed documentation (e.g., exact search queries, list of channels) to enhance reproducibility.

strengths: The paper addresses a significant and practical challenge in computer vision for ecology: the lack of high-quality, large-scale domain-specific video datasets for non-human primates, reducing reliance on human-centric representations.

The data curation pipeline is solid and well-engineered, combining cut detection, CLIP-based relevance filtering, zero-shot detection (using Grounding DINO), and metadata-guided subsampling to yield a high-quality 424-hour dataset.

The proposed deep but narrow attentive classifier (using dimension downprojection and multi-CLS tokens) is technically sound. It effectively addresses the overfitting problem typical of standard, overparameterized classification heads on small-scale animal behavioral datasets.

The experiments are thorough, spanning four distinct benchmark datasets (PanAf500, ChimpACT, BaboonLand, ChimpBehave) representing different settings (wild, zoo, drone). The method consistently outperforms strong baselines and large foundation models like VideoPrism.

Ablation studies are detailed and clearly isolate the impact of different dataset components (YT-Filtered vs. YT-Random), the value of primate-centric cropping during pretraining, and the design choices of the attentive classifier.
weaknesses: There is a limitation regarding full reproducibility: 14% of the R&O dataset cannot be publicly shared due to data privacy/ongoing research agreements. While common in ecology, this restricts complete dataset replication.

The evaluation protocol relies heavily on ground-truth bounding boxes for cropping primates during downstream inference. A more realistic evaluation would include end-to-end testing with predicted bounding boxes from a detector to assess how the classification performance degrades under noisy localization.

The taxonomic distribution of the dataset is highly skewed, with Macaques and Chimpanzees accounting for over 62% of the data, while other families (e.g., Lemuridae, Marmosets, Orangutans) are relatively underrepresented. This imbalance might limit the model's true generalization capacity across the entire primate order.

strengths: Addresses a critical gap in computer vision for ecological and conservation applications by shifting from human-centric models to a dedicated primate-centric foundation model.

Presents a well-structured and scalable data curation pipeline that leverages automated cut detection, zero-shot detection (Grounding DINO), and active-filtered YouTube retrieval to compile 424 hours of high-quality primate video data.
Proposes a novel, lightweight, and narrow-but-deep attentive classifier specifically designed to mitigate overfitting when evaluating frozen backbones on small downstream animal behavior datasets.

Exhibits strong empirical results, achieving state-of-the-art performance across four distinct primate behavior benchmarks and demonstrating highly favorable data efficiency during downstream adaptation.

Provides extensive and insightful ablation studies validating the individual components of the curation pipeline, the importance of primate-centric cropping, and the specific design choices of the classifier head.
weaknesses: A portion of the research data (14% of the dataset containing camera trap footage from ongoing research) cannot be shared publicly, which slightly limits the exact reproduction of the full PriVi dataset.

The model relies heavily on cropped bounding boxes of primates; while this is standard for the evaluated action recognition protocols, a fully end-to-end framework integrating joint detection, tracking, and behavior analysis in the wild remains to be explored.

The dataset representation is skewed towards certain genus/family types (e.g., Macaques and Chimpanzees constitute over 60% of the dataset), while other primate species have significantly less coverage.
